108.0.0.en: 1 O God, my heart is fixed; I will sing and give praise, even with my glory. 2 Awake, psaltery and harp: I myself will awake early. 3 I will praise thee, O LORD, among the people: and I will sing praises unto thee among the nations. 4 For thy mercy is great above the heavens: and thy truth reacheth unto the clouds. 5 Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens: and thy glory above all the earth.

108.0.1.en: The psalm begins with a hymn of praise to God, in which the psalmist finds refuge and steadfastness in the heart of God. It is a hymn of victory over all the troubles of danger.

108.0.2.en: O God, my heart is fixed.

108.0.3.en: I will sing and give praise,

108.0.5.en: The Septuagint and Coptic versions read: "My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready. I will sing and chant praise in my glory".

108.1.0.en: * "My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready." I am ready not only in deed, but also in heart and mind. My heart is ready in desire; my heart is ready to serve by deed [3].

108.1.1.en: * "I will sing and chant praise in my glory." Simply, it means that when I praise You with a melody, O Lord, when I chant to You, I offer You no benefit; it is for me alone. In truth, another psalm says: [You have no need of my goodness] (See Ps 16:2). Therefore what I do, I do for my own good. When I serve You, this is a glory to me.

108.1.2.en: We fast; do we give God anything? We do this for the sake of our sins.

108.2.0.en: We sleep on sackcloth. What does God do with this? Only one thing: we save our souls, and this is what He desires. As a good and gentle physician rejoices in his patient when he heals him, so our Lord does [4].

108.2.1.en: St. Jerome *The prophet repeated the words "my heart is ready" twice, because if one who is determined to receive a king in his house prepares two things, first cleaning it of filth, and second adorning it with the most precious and finest furnishings, so also he who is about to receive Christ at once into his heart must cleanse it by confessing his sins, and beautify it with the adornment of good and righteous works. Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God, and they praise and chant to Him in their glory, I mean in their intellectual and practical virtues, which glorify and honor them in this world and in the next. Also their glory will be Christ, who, when He took what is ours, made us the like of His image and partakers of His glory.

108.3.2.en: The Septuagint and Coptic versions read: "Awake, my glory! Awake, psaltery and harp! Awake at the time of dawn".

108.3.3.en: The psalmist wants to praise God at dawn, before the rising of the sun, affirming that the night did not hinder him from thinking about God's dealings with His people as well as with himself personally, so he offers the firstfruits of his day to praise and thanksgiving to God.

108.3.4.en: St. Jerome sees that the address here is also from the incarnate Son to the Father. By His incarnation the Word of God declares that He bears the harp of His becoming man, on which to play the melody of divine love toward all mankind. His soul went down to Hades playing the melody of victory, releasing the souls of those who had fallen asleep in hope, freeing them from bondage, and leading them to Paradise.

108.4.0.en: * As the psaltery has many strings, and if one string is broken the whole instrument becomes useless, so also in our deeds: if we disobey one commandment, our psaltery is broken [5].

108.5.0.en: * If you are a psaltery, if you are a harp, why are you silent and do not glorify God? "Awake at the time of dawn." There is no blessing or praise of God in darkness, but in light. I want to say something awesome. Even if we rise in the night, it is to bless God in the light. For the Christian has no night, but the Sun of Righteousness is always shining for him [6].

108.6.0.en: * According to another interpretation, the Lord Himself says: "My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready. I am ready here; and I am ready in the world to come. I am a Savior on earth; and I am a Savior in heaven. I give eternal life to both angels and men. "Awake, psaltery and harp." The Lord speaks to His body: Psaltery and harp, you who went down to Hades and rested, awake and glorify the Lord. Be sure that you understand what I say. It is not he who holds the psaltery and harp who praises, but the psaltery and harp themselves praise the Father. It is the Father, who is blessed and praised by others, whereas the body (of Christ) and His humanity that He took praise the Lord [7].

108.6.1.en: St. Jerome *By saying, "Awake, my glory," he urges and raises up the spirit of prophecy that was in him to glorify Him with spiritual glory. And by saying psaltery and harp he raises up the powers of his soul and the senses of his body, so that both sides may agree in praising God in harmony and union, and for receiving the Holy Spirit. He also raises up the Old and New Testaments, so that in one accord they may proclaim the works of the incarnation of our Lord. For the Old Testament contains foreknowledge of what was to be, while the New Testament proclaims the fulfillment of the prophecies. His saying "early" makes clear the time at which the Sun of Righteousness, who is our Lord Jesus Christ, arose; I mean the time of His incarnation, because David from that time until the end praises and chants to God with us who have been enlightened and who walk as in a good day.

108.6.2.en: Hesychius said: When the prophet urged Christ, saying, "Awake, my glory," our Lord's answer to him is, as it were: Yes, I awake, and I rise from the dead as from an early sleep.

108.7.0.en: I will praise thee, O LORD, among the people: and I will sing praises unto thee among the nations [3].

108.7.1.en: The Septuagint and Coptic versions read: "I will confess You among the peoples, O Lord, and I will chant to You among the nations".

108.7.2.en: *It is as though the psalmist joins us who believe in Christ, for when we recite what he sings, he has praised and chanted to God with us among the peoples concerning the salvation that the Lord Christ accomplished.

108.8.0.en: For thy mercy is great above the heavens: and thy truth reacheth unto the clouds [4].

108.8.1.en: The Septuagint and Coptic versions read: "For Your mercy is great above the heavens, and Your truth unto the cloud".

108.8.2.en: * There is no creature that does not depend on God's tenderness. Each one of us needs God's compassion. Gabriel and Michael, the seraphim and cherubim, the powers and authorities, all are truly holy, yet they stand in need of the mercies of their Creator. I am not belittling the angels, but proclaiming their Creator, for the angels themselves offer Him glory of their own free will and with joy.

108.8.3.en: We can also express the thought carried by this phrase in another way: Your tenderness lifts us from earth to heaven. "And Your truth unto the clouds"... How does God's truth reach heaven? The Son of God says: "I am the way, the truth, and the life" (Jn 14:6). And He came down to earth and conversed with men (Bar 3:38). How then is God's truth in the clouds? It is quite clear that the prophet is referring to the apostles and the saints.

108.9.0.en: "Great above the heavens." God is not magnified on earth. For as long as we are earthly we do not magnify God, but when we are changed from earthly to heavenly we magnify God [8].

108.9.1.en: St. Jerome *His saying, "Your mercy is great above the heavens and unto the clouds," means that Your mercy is wider and broader than the heaven, and covers all our sins from above. And that the beginning of mercy is on earth and its end is in heaven.

108.9.2.en: I mean that You show mercy to the people who are on earth, as it is written that the earth is full of Your mercy, and the end of those who are shown mercy is to reach heaven.

108.9.3.en: As for his saying "unto the clouds" concerning the prophets and apostles, it is because they are lofty and noble, and because God rains down His teachings to water people through His apostles and prophets...

108.9.4.en: The prophet's saying, "Your mercy is great in the heavens," means that the angels magnify His divinity above the heavens. Also, He revealed His greatness and majesty to all when You ascended into the heavens, for humanity veiled Him when You were on earth; I mean, before Your ascension to heaven people did not know the greatness of Your divinity. But now they know that You are a great God in the heavens and glorified.

108.10.0.en: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens: and thy glory above all the earth [5].

108.10.1.en: In the spirit of prophecy the psalmist saw the Lord Christ ascending into heaven, and his soul rejoiced, sharing with the disciples who returned from the Mount of Olives to Jerusalem with great joy.

108.10.2.en: The psalmist realized that he shares in praise with the men of the New Testament, for he now has a store laid up in heaven.

108.10.3.en: By the ascension of the Lord Christ, the Head of the universal Church, the whole body, made up of God's people in the Old and New Testaments, gained the right to go forth to heaven.

108.10.4.en: The psalmist realized that he was in wondrous glory, for he was being raised from the dust and the dunghill to sit with the nobles of the nobles of his people, that is, with the heavenly orders.

108.10.5.en: *This saying contains a prophecy of the ascension of our Lord Jesus Christ into the heavens.

108.10.6.en: *By His ascension and the sending of His Holy Spirit He saved His beloved, I mean the people for whose sake, out of His love for them, He came down and became incarnate and saved them from Satan.

108.11.s.en: 2. God the hope of His people

108.11.0.en: 6 That thy beloved may be delivered: save with thy right hand, and answer me. 7 God hath spoken in his holiness; "I will rejoice, I will divide Shechem, and mete out the valley of Succoth. 8 Gilead is mine; Manasseh is mine; Ephraim also is the helmet of my head; Judah is my sceptre. 9 Moab is my washpot; over Edom will I cast out my shoe; O Philistia, shout aloud over me." 10 Who will bring me into the strong city? who will lead me into Edom? 11 Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off? and wilt not thou, O God, go forth with our hosts? 12 Give us help from trouble: for vain is the help of man. 13 Through God we shall do valiantly: for he it is that shall tread down our enemies.

108.11.1.en: Despite the dangers through which the people pass, their hope in God pours upon them a spirit of joy, not only upon obtaining victory, but from the moment the calamity begins. For God, as the leader of His people, carries them across to certain victory. The people rest and hide amid dangers in the heart of God, which is wide with love.

108.11.2.en: That thy beloved may be delivered:

108.11.3.en: save with thy right hand, and answer me [6].

108.12.0.en: *Therefore the Church says by the tongue of the elect: "His left hand is under my head, and his right hand doth embrace me" (Song 2:6). The Church rests her head under God's left hand, as though meaning by this the good things of earthly life, and she rests on them with the joy of surpassing love. But God's right hand, which embraces her, means that eternal joy surrounds her on every side. Therefore Solomon also says: "Length of days is in her right hand; and in her left hand riches and honour" (Prov 3:16). Here Solomon shows that riches and honor appear as though inscribed on the left hand. So the psalmist says: "Save with thy right hand, and answer me" (Ps 108:6). Here he refers to the right hand, because he means that he asks for eternal salvation. Therefore it is also written: "Thy right hand, O LORD, hath dashed in pieces the enemy" (Ex 15:6). God's enemies may enjoy good things by God's left hand, but God's right hand destroys them. For we usually see the wicked exalted in earthly life, but at the coming of eternal glory the curse falls upon them [9].

108.13.0.en: God hath spoken in his holiness;

108.13.1.en: I will rejoice, I will divide Shechem, and mete out the valley of Succoth [7].

108.13.2.en: This salvation does not only gladden the hearts of the believers, but God Himself says: "I will rejoice." He delights in the salvation of mankind, and in the victory of the believers there is glory for Him, for He rejoices in them and in their victory through Him.

108.13.3.en: St. Jerome sees that the secret of the psalmist's praise and the exultation of his heart is God's delight in salvation. There is nothing in which the Father delights as He does in the Cross of the Lord of glory Jesus, where divine love was realized in its most splendid form. The Father rejoiced in the Cross of His only-begotten Son.

108.13.4.en: The works of the Cross and its efficacy remain the secret of our constant praise, where we find our happiness in sharing with the Crucified the sufferings of love, and in being lifted up by the Cross above every temporal concern.

108.13.5.en: St. Jerome also sees that the manifold fruits of the Cross have become the song that he sings:

108.13.6.en: a. I will divide Shechem: St. Jerome sees that Shechem means "shoulders"; if the Lord Christ in His love bent His back to carry the Cross on His shoulders for us with all joy, He granted us also to carry the Cross with Him on our shoulders as a sweet and joyful yoke.

108.13.7.en: b. I will mete out the valley of tents (Succoth): where Christ grants His saints who have enjoyed His Cross the knowledge of His mysteries while still on earth, but each according to his stature or measure.

108.14.0.en: * "God hath spoken in his holiness," whether in the temple, or in one of His saints, or in the prophet. He was heard in Moses, and was heard in the Apostle, and truly I say He has spoken in His Son. What did God promise? What followed: "I will rejoice, I will divide Shechem." He says: For this I was crucified, that I may distribute Shechem. "Shechem" in our language means "shoulders." And shoulders, on the other hand, are used for work. The meaning then: the purpose of my crucifixion is to share my work with my saints. For this I was crucified, to put my sweet yoke and my light burden on the shoulders of men. This You do, O Lord, as You promised; You are glorified and Shechem is divided [10].

108.15.0.en: * "And mete out the valley of tents." Truly our Lord and Savior entered this valley of tears, the place of our humility, in this world. Yet the saint in this world still does not know what befits him as he ought, "for we know in part, and we prophesy in part" (1 Cor 13:9) [11].

108.15.1.en: St. Jerome *The spiritual meaning is that "Shechem" is interpreted "the exalted." The One exalted above worldly things is the Holy Spirit, who divided His gifts among the believers after the ascension of our Lord Jesus Christ into heaven, and measured and apportioned them to each one according to his worthiness.

108.15.2.en: As for the valley of shadows (Succoth), it is said of the whole inhabited world, in which the lands are pitched like tents; He made them portions for the heads of the churches, that each one may manage what his church comprises.

108.16.0.en: Gilead is mine; Manasseh is mine;

108.16.1.en: Ephraim also is the helmet of my head;

108.16.3.en: St. Jerome sees that the Lord Christ rejoices also in the fruit of His Cross, for He has gained great riches, not out of need of anything, but for the sake of the salvation of mankind and its enjoyment of what is to come:

108.16.4.en: a. "Gilead is mine": since Gilead means "emigration," the Gentiles emigrated to Him, or returned to Him after living in the humiliation of bondage to the devil. They returned with the spirit of freedom, rejoicing, and their Savior rejoiced over them.

108.16.5.en: b. "Manasseh is mine": for it had previously forgotten God's fatherhood to it. And now it has returned to Him, remembering His love for it.

108.16.6.en: c. "Judah is my sceptre": mankind came to be in royal glory, belonging to the King of kings, after it became "Judah," that is, "confession," confessing the mercies of God who forgives sins.

108.16.7.en: * "Gilead is mine, Manasseh is mine." Our Lord and Savior rejoices, because He has much wealth. The meaning of "Gilead" is "emigration." He rejoices because the Gentiles have emigrated to Him. "Manasseh" means "forgetfulness," and accordingly we understand: this son who took his inheritance and squandered it and forgot all that concerns me remembers me now. I call him Manasseh, that is, from forgetfulness, because he forgets but returns to his father.

108.16.8.en: "Ephraim" is interpreted "fruitful"; He says: "Ephraim is the helmet of my head." Here He uses the helmet instead of the crown, because what is placed on the head is the wreath. And the Holy Scripture uses many expressions concerning the wreath...

108.17.0.en: Notice what the psalm says: you have become Gilead, you have become Manasseh, he emigrated to the Lord, and after your forgetfulness you returned to your Father. Be Ephraim also, that is, be fruitful, practicing good works, and afterward you become the crown of the Lord [12].

108.18.0.en: * "Judah is my sceptre." Think of the greatness of the glory that awaits the penitent; now Judah means "confession" [13].

108.18.1.en: St. Jerome *The word "Gilead" is interpreted "transfer," "Manasseh" means "forgetfulness," "Ephraim" means "abundance of fruit," and "Judah" is interpreted "the confessor"... This indicates that Christ says after His ascension into heaven: Everyone who has passed from unbelief to faith submits to Me, and whoever has forgotten his former evil works, and whoever bears abundant fruit by working virtues, he rules over the enemies, and the confessor becomes a king like Me... As for the sons of Moab, who were forbidden to enter the temple, they are about to become My own through the washing of holy Baptism.

108.19.1.en: over Edom will I cast out my shoe;

108.19.2.en: O Philistia, shout aloud over me [9].

108.19.3.en: The text in the Septuagint and Coptic versions reads: "Moab is the vessel of my hope".

108.19.4.en: Moab, together with Edom and Ammon, was among the fiercest enemies of Israel. And the Law came commanding that none of the Moabites and the Amorites should enter the congregation of the Lord until the tenth generation (Deut 23:3-6). But the psalmist, having lifted his eyes to the Cross, saw Moab enjoying the waters of Baptism (the washpot) that belong to the Lord, so that they become sons of God, the object of His pleasure.

108.19.5.en: Moab, who was the fruit of the sin of Lot with his daughter, a symbol of uncleanness, represents Satan; he enjoyed reconciliation with God, and left his sonship to the devil to live in the bosom of the Lord. This is the chosen vessel for which the Lord hopes by the power of His Cross.

108.19.6.en: Edom, which means blood or earth, refers to the first Adam, fallen because of his rebellion against God, who enjoyed the descent of the Word of God incarnate, and lives in the midst of mankind that He may unite him to Himself.

108.19.7.en: As for Philistia, which was in continual resistance to His people, opposing the worship of the true God, when it believes in the crucified Christ it is turned into a chorus of acclamation.

108.19.8.en: Thus the Church of Christ became the holy Bride from all nations, peoples, and tongues.

108.19.9.en: Eusebius sees that the shoe refers to the Incarnation; for this reason John the Baptist said that he was not worthy to loose the latchet of His shoe, that is, to explain the mystery of His Incarnation. So over Edom He casts His shoe, that is, the Lord Christ walks with the preaching of His holy Gospel over the Gentile lands and foreign tribes such as Edom, which means earth.

108.19.10.en: * "Moab is the cauldron (washpot) of my hope." What a great mystery we learn from these few words... For Moab is translated "from the father"... Who is this man who is from the father? He who loses his father, who left him and did not return to him, so he is not worthy to be called Manasseh.

108.19.11.en: Who is Moab? An enemy of the Lord, whose kind, even to the fourth and tenth generation, indeed to the end of the world, does not enter the Church of the Lord.

108.19.12.en: Who is Moab? He who is born in the pit of darkness from an unclean union. From the union of Lot with his two daughters two sons were born: Moab is the elder... in the darkness in a cave, and not in the sun and the light; for this reason Moab is the other name of Satan, who does not think of his father. Truly Absalom, who persecuted his father, also represents the devil.

108.19.13.en: But in what sense is Moab called the washpot of the hope of the Lord...? The Apostle says: "Whom I have delivered unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme" (1 Tim 1:20).

108.19.14.en: Satan is, as it appears, the Lord's means of discipline. Those who do not walk toward God in righteousness are delivered to Satan... until they return to (the Lord)...

108.19.15.en: "Over Edom will I cast out my shoe." "Edom" means "from the earth," and "from the blood." The God of love and tenderness lays claim not only to the heavenly but also to the earthly. The Philistines become my friends. He says this about us who believe and were from the Gentiles [14].

108.19.16.en: St. Jerome *The nation of Moab submits to them, and becomes like a basin for washing their feet, and their feet extend to the land of Edom, and the neighboring foreign nations submit to them.

108.20.0.en: Who will bring me into the strong city?

108.20.1.en: Who will lead me into Edom? [10].

108.20.2.en: The psalmist longs to see the Church of the New Testament, the fortified city, and to be guided to Edom, which had been estranged by its worship of idols and came to bear the preaching of the divine Incarnation. The Lord Himself, the secret of her strength, rejoices in her, saying: "Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners?" (Song 6:10).

108.20.3.en: St. Jerome sees the fortified city as Hades, which whoever enters cannot leave. The men of the Old Testament entered it and could not leave it. It is said of Jacob: "And he refused to be comforted; and he said, For I will go down into the grave unto my son mourning. Thus his father wept for him" (Gen 37:35) (that is, for his son Joseph). Hades had an entrance, but it had no exit. One alone entered Hades and came out victorious, our Lord Jesus Christ!

108.20.4.en: David the psalmist, like all the men of the Old Testament, feared death, because Hades awaited them, but the Cross of the Lord of glory Jesus shattered the bars of Hades and emptied it of those who died in hope of God's wonderful salvation!

108.21.0.en: Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off? and wilt not thou, O God, go forth with our hosts? [11].

108.21.1.en: It is good for a man to work and strive like a mighty army, but without the grace of God he becomes rejected, and it is in vain that he enjoys victory.

108.21.2.en: God is a refuge for us in the midst of our distress; by His grace He leads all our energies and turns our hearts into a Jerusalem like an army with banners (Song 6:4), which no powers of darkness can storm.

108.21.3.en: * Notice the prophet's words carefully. He did not say: You go forth, but "and wilt not thou, O God, go forth with our hosts?" The prophet's teaching is this: when we exert effort, God helps us. So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy (Rom 9:16). Do you understand that this saying means: it is not of him who rests, nor of him who sleeps, but of God who shows mercy...? On our part we must will and run; then He has compassion on us. When the wrestler sleeps he loses the victory [15].

108.22.1.en: for vain is the help of man [12].

108.22.2.en: We often murmur in time of distress, and we even see in the writings of the Fathers, such as the Conferences of St. John Cassian, that one of the Fathers was asked: Why does God allow tribulations for the saints?

108.22.3.en: Affliction, as St. Augustine sees it, comes by God's permission for our edification, for we do not taste God's mercies and His care for us and touch His love as we do when affliction comes upon us, so we cry out to God and discover that He is a refuge for us in our distress.

108.22.4.en: * Do you want the Lord to hear you with tenderness? While you are in distress, call upon Him, and He will answer you kindly. Unless a person is in distress he cannot call upon the Lord for help. Vain is the help of men. [Cursed be the man that trusteth in man] (See Jer 17:5) [16].

108.23.0.en: Through God we shall do valiantly:

108.23.1.en: for he it is that shall tread down our enemies [13].

108.23.2.en: Through the literal Law, man did not enjoy salvation but was in distress; but now that the Word of God has come incarnate, He has given us the spirit of power and of victory over the devil and his angels, our true enemies.

108.23.3.en: * "Through God we shall do valiantly" [13]. Let us put our trust in God alone... Christ is with you; are you still afraid? If He feeds the birds of heaven, do you doubt His power to feed you also? Does Satan feed his men, and Christ not feed His servants...? Let us cast out all anxiety from our hearts, and say: "Through God we shall do valiantly." He will be our bread, He will be our king. "He it is that shall tread down our enemies." He crowns, He fights with us at our side, and more than this, He wins the victory in us... When we are courageous He treads down our enemies. Scripture did not say that He fights or kills, but that He treads down our enemies [17].

108.23.5.en: Your praise fills my whole being with Your glory!

108.23.6.en: *In the midst of my distress I take refuge in You, for You are the faithful refuge.

108.23.7.en: My heart is filled with Your peace, and my depths rejoice in You.

108.23.8.en: And my body sets out to work and service by Your Holy Spirit.

108.23.9.en: I have truly realized why the heavenly ones live in a feast that never ends!

108.23.10.en: For You have no need of anyone's praise; rather, praise of You fills the being of Your creation with inexpressible joy!

108.23.11.en: *I say with the psalmist: My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready.

108.23.12.en: By Your grace my heart has hated all defilement and uncleanness, and has become a royal palace in which You dwell.

108.23.13.en: You pour upon it from the abundance of Your grace, and the fragrance of Your holiness spreads in it!

108.23.14.en: You fill it with the treasures of Your glory, and adorn it with Your wondrous splendor!

108.23.15.en: Allow me to proclaim with all power?

108.23.16.en: Your indwelling fills my tongue with praise, and overflows with Your glory upon my depths!

108.23.17.en: You are my glory, my satisfaction, and my unceasing joy!

108.23.18.en: *As I meditate on Your love, the darkness of night is turned into wondrous light!

108.23.19.en: The body sleeps and rests, but Your light fills my depths with splendor.

108.23.20.en: At dawn, at the rising of the sun, I take the psaltery and the harp.

108.23.21.en: Play upon the strings of my soul that rejoices in You.

108.23.22.en: For all that is within me finds its delight in praising You!

108.23.23.en: *By Your incarnation the dawn has come upon us, O Sun of Righteousness.

108.23.24.en: So our souls, together with our bodies, set out praising You in wondrous harmony.

108.23.25.en: *By Your becoming man You came down to us; You turned our life into a unique harp, on which You play with the Spirit of divine love, and You grant us the risen life, ever rejoicing and praising.

108.23.26.en: *How wondrous! The psalmist enjoyed the spirit of prophecy.

108.23.27.en: He saw You risen to gather the peoples together into Your rejoicing Church.

108.23.28.en: He went forth to sing to You among the peoples coming to You.

108.23.29.en: He beheld Your Church having become a new heaven.

108.23.30.en: So he realized that Your mercy has lifted the earthly ones on high.

108.23.31.en: Men join with the heavenly orders in praising You.

108.23.32.en: I proclaim Your glory in men who have become almost heavenly.

108.23.33.en: They rose up from the dunghill and sat with the upper orders in heaven!

108.23.34.en: *Your Cross is the fountain of praise and joy.

108.23.35.en: The Father rejoices and exults, seeing mankind regain its beauty.

108.23.36.en: Mankind bowed its shoulders and began to praise:

108.23.37.en: I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me.

108.23.38.en: It enjoyed the knowledge of the mysteries of heaven, each according to his measure.

108.23.39.en: It emigrated to Him, for it was freed from bondage to the devil.

108.23.40.en: It returned remembering the kindnesses of its heavenly Father, after having previously forgotten His fatherhood and squandered its inheritance.

108.23.41.en: It began to confess His mercy and to find its glory in Him.

108.23.42.en: It was washed in the waters of Baptism, and enjoyed the spirit of adoption.

108.23.43.en: *By Your Cross You acquired Your Church from all peoples.

108.23.44.en: From the tribes of Israel, such as Gilead, Manasseh, Ephraim, and Judah, those who emigrated to You, where they understood the prophecies, left the letter of the Law and received it by the life-giving Spirit.

108.23.45.en: They became kings with authority, over whom the devil, the opponent of the truth, has no power.

108.23.46.en: From the Gentiles, Moab, Edom, Philistia, and others enjoyed membership in Your holy Body.

108.23.47.en: The spirit of enmity departed from them and they were kindled with holy zeal.

108.23.48.en: They left vanities and the worship of idols, and accepted Your true divine Cross.

108.23.49.en: Your Cross turned Hades into a wondrous spectacle!

108.23.50.en: We stand before it, which had imprisoned the souls of all, with its gates shattered and its bars collapsed.

108.23.51.en: Those who were as in an eternal prison came out, rejoicing in You, O Conqueror of Hades and Giver of eternity!

108.23.53.en: It turned our hearts into the awesome Jerusalem, like an army with banners.

108.23.54.en: You became the commander of the battle against the devil, and gave us the spirit of power and certainty in Your victory!

108.23.55.en: We no longer fear the enemy, for the devil falls like lightning from heaven.

108.23.56.en: You gave us authority to tread on serpents and scorpions and over all the power of the enemy!

108.23.57.en: Glory to You, O Crucified One, Giver of glory and power!
